metadata.description: A physical machine as a managed ASSET (the box itself) — the raw-resource form of compute. It can exist unallocated in inventory (lifecycle_state: available, §28), carries aggregate hardware capacity (cpu/memory/storage/gpu) as host attributes (§26; ADR-013 — components are not separate records), and is the thing that hosts workloads (VMs, containers, OSDs). An ALLOCATION of a host to a consumer is NOT a separate type — it is the Ownership/Allocation model (docs/spec/foundations/ownership-sharing-allocation.md §2.1 whole-allocation); a running 'instance' is a realized entity of this type. Grounded in Redfish ComputerSystem (inventory/system) + Metal3 BareMetalHost (provisioning lifecycle).
metadata.converted_from: flat spec Compute.BareMetalHost@0.8.0 (bulk mechanical conversion 2026-08-04; factoring later via scope promotion)

instance_size.description: Provider-neutral size class (small|medium|large, ordered/comparable — common-elements §2.2, ADR-014). Size by class IN PLACE OF cpu+memory; the provider maps it to concrete resources at naturalization (ADR-023). anyOf enforces sizing by class OR raw.

cpu.description: Reconciled CPU rollup (§26) — aggregate host CPU. Adopts Redfish ProcessorSummary.

memory.description: Reconciled memory rollup (§26) — aggregate host memory. Adopts Redfish MemorySummary.

storage.description: Reconciled local-storage rollup (§26) — aggregate host local storage.

storage_tier.description: The requested storage performance class — a GOVERNED vocabulary (ADR-038 §2): canonical terms are `storage_tier` reference-data records (standard/performance/archive), each denoting a requirements floor. Name-selectable but requirements-authoritative (ADR-036); profile decides bare string vs data_reference (ADR-007/ADR-039). Mirrors the Compute Base Class `storage_tier` element. Governed vocabulary `storage_tier` (ADR-038 §2); name-selectable but requirements-authoritative (ADR-036). Profile decides bare-vs-reference.

guest_os.description: Guest operating system. Portable form is a reference to an os_image reference-data vocabulary (ADR-012; layering §3.7) the target provider advertises via capability discovery (ADR-004); policy validates membership at request. Inline is the portability_breaking escape. Optional at the data layer (bare-instantiation philosophy): a VM may be declared by sizing alone; a profile MAY require it.

type.description: Inline OS identifier (e.g. linux-server-9). portability_breaking: a value with no os_image vocabulary entry — a review finding.

lifecycle_state.description: Allocation state (common-elements §6, §28). available = inventoried/unallocated raw asset; allocated = adopted into the managed lifecycle. Adopts Metal3 BareMetalHost.status.provisioning.state.

composition_visibility.description: Whether the host's kept components (Hardware.NetworkInterface) are modeled as first-class entities vs a rollup (§26, docs/spec/foundations/service-dependencies.md §11d); memory/CPU/disk/GPU are aggregate host attributes, not component records (ADR-013). opaque = rollup only.

image.description: The provisioning image for this host (Metal3 image): what gets written to the root device at provision time. A host rebuilt from intent re-provisions from exactly this image.

url.description: Image URL (artifact location, not a resource reference).

root_device_hints.description: Which disk receives the image (Metal3 rootDeviceHints, the portable core) — the §27 Identity discriminators in provisioning form, matched at provision time.

serial_number.description: Disk serial hint — the stable choice across reboots.

boot_mac_address.description: The NIC MAC the host network-boots from (Metal3 bootMACAddress) — ties provisioning to a concrete port; pairs with that NIC's Hardware.NetworkInterface record.

online.description: Desired power target (Metal3 online): true = powered on and kept on. The intent counterpart of the observed power_state output — the host analogue of the VM's run_state.desired_state.

boot_mode.description: Firmware boot mode (Metal3 bootMode / Redfish Boot). Fleet note: converging this with the VM's firmware block into a common element is a candidate next MINOR — adopted vocabulary kept verbatim until then.

power_state.description: Observed power state — On | Off | PoweringOn | PoweringOff (Redfish ComputerSystem.PowerState). Drives shutdown/startup ordering for the dependency graph.

management_address.description: Reachable management endpoint (BMC/Redfish or host management IP) once Realized. When a Hardware.BMC record exists for this host, the BMC record is authoritative; this output is the convenience copy.

provisioning_state.description: Metal3's headline status (available | provisioning | provisioned | deprovisioning | error) — the signal cluster bring-up binds on: a Cluster/NodePool consumer waits for provisioned.

os_image_digest.description: Content digest of the OS image the host actually runs — the Realized twin of spec.image.checksum. Answers 'which hosts run which image, and which have never converged?' from declared outputs: season-pin != os_image_digest is the derivable never-converged / stale-image fact, without restating the image record.

effective_config_digest.description: Digest of the resolved effective configuration this host last converged to — the Realized twin of the assembled request. The comparable fact only: per-field values and their winning layers are reconstructable from the layer chain + provenance (LAY-008), never restated here. Pairs with os_image_digest to make requested-vs-realized configuration a first-class, bindable comparison per host.

relationships.description: Power source(s) the host draws from; the host stops before the feed in a reverse-topo shutdown.
The desired BIOS/firmware profile this host converges to (drift = live BIOS != profile). Host-side declaration per the dependent-side rule.

adopts.role: physical system inventory + power vocabulary (identity, processor/memory summary, PowerState)

context.purpose: Models a physical machine as a managed asset — the box itself, whether or not anything is running on it yet.
context.plain_description: One physical server: its identity (serial, model, asset tag), its aggregate capacity (CPU sockets and cores, memory, local storage), and its lifecycle state. It can sit unallocated in inventory before anything is deployed on it. Components like NICs can be modeled as their own records attached to the host; CPU, memory, and disk normally stay as rollup numbers on the host itself. Everything that runs — VMs, containers, storage daemons — ultimately sits on one of these, which makes it a central node in shutdown and startup ordering.
use_when: You need an inventory of physical servers, including ones not yet assigned to any workload.
You need the dependency chain workload → host → power feed, so an outage or maintenance walk knows what stops when.
You need per-host aggregate capacity (cores, memory, storage) for allocation decisions.
you need host provisioning to be replayable intent — image, root device, boot MAC, power target — so a lost host rebuilds from the estate (the bare-metal leg of rehydration)
not_for: A virtual machine — that is Compute.VM; a host is hardware you can touch.
The host's out-of-band management controller — that is Hardware.BMC, its own record with its own address and power-control surface.
Individual NICs, GPUs, or drives inside the host — those are Hardware.NetworkInterface / Hardware.GraphicsProcessor / Hardware.StorageDevice records contained by the host.
works_with: Facility.PowerFeed — the power source the host draws from; roots the shutdown ordering.
Hardware.BiosProfile — the firmware configuration the host converges to.
Hardware.NetworkInterface — the host's NICs, modeled as contained components.
Compute.VM — the guests the host runs.
